stories.title: Trump waives Russia sanctions law, drawing bipartisan criticism
stories.summary: Late on Friday, October 16, President Trump issued an executive order waiving implementation of the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, which Congress passed last month and which would have imposed broad sanctions on Russia and on countries buying Russian oil. Leaders in both parties criticized the waiver on Saturday, including Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and Republican Sen. Thom Tillis. The White House defended the move, saying it gives the president more authority to pursue a peace agreement between Russia and Ukraine. Lawmakers are expected to revisit the issue when Congress returns for its lame-duck session.

stories.title: US stocks mixed as tech rebounds; oil eases from five-month high
stories.summary: At the opening bell on October 19, the S&P 500 rose 0.57% and the Nasdaq 1.09%, while the Dow slipped 0.08% and the Russell 2000 fell 1.66%, as tech and AI shares bounced after Friday's sell-off tied to doubts over returns on AI capital spending. WTI crude fell 0.88% to $100.50 and Brent fell 1.47% to $108.20, easing from a five-month high after the Russia sanctions waiver. NAHB builder sentiment dropped three points to 29, its lowest since June 2012, with the 30-year mortgage rate averaging 7.40%. Meta, Tesla, IBM, Netflix, GM and AT&T report earnings this week.

stories.title: Anthropic creates Public Benefit Fund backed by company shares
stories.summary: Anthropic announced the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a wholly-owned LLC that will initially hold 5% of the company's shares, subject to stockholder approval. The board may add 2% for every 50% increase in company value above a set baseline. Anthropic says roughly 20% of its shares are now dedicated to the public good once earlier founder and employee equity pledges are counted, and that the fund's equity will not be used for lobbying or political giving. The company says it will share more on structure and governance in coming months.

stories.title: Evidence suggests second supermassive black hole in galaxy Mrk 501
stories.summary: Researchers at the Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy report detecting a second particle jet in the core of galaxy Mrk 501, using radio observations spanning about 23 years. The jet points to a hidden second black hole orbiting the first roughly every 121 days, at a separation of 250 to 540 times the Earth-Sun distance. Each black hole is estimated at 100 million to 1 billion solar masses, and depending on their masses they could merge in as little as 100 years. The work was published in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society.
